metadataReview.note: The inherited record has no coordinates. The Shipka–Buzludzha National Park-Museum describes the fighting of 8–9 January 1878 for the fortified Ottoman camp near Shipka and Sheynovo, with Radetzky’s frontal attack on the pass as a separate sector. The point is placed at Redoubt No. 1 on the Golyama Kosmatka mound, which Kazanlak Municipality identifies as the key work of the Sheynovo camp and Vessel Pasha’s command post. It does not represent the pass positions or the flanking columns. The existing dates are retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred from these sources.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: Kazanlak Municipality states that Redoubt No. 1, the most important part of the Sheynovo fortified camp and Vessel Pasha’s command post during the two days of fighting in January 1878, stood at the Golyama Kosmatka mound between Shipka and Sheynovo. OpenStreetMap way 203172707, tagged as the Golyama Kosmatka tumulus and linked to Wikidata Q3992623, has the Nominatim centroid latitude 42.7001058, longitude 25.3334304, rounded to [25.3334,42.7001]; Wikidata gives 42.6999, 25.3334 for the same mound. This is a redoubt-sector reference inside the fortified camp, not the position of an attacking column, the Shipka Pass front or the full extent of the operation. The later Victory Monument near Sheynovo is not used, and no accuracy radius is claimed.
